proved_step: PROOF. Fix a prefix a in {0,1}^l and write theta_i(a) = t_i - W_i1 . a. The residual of g_i is y -> [W_i2 . y >= theta_i(a)], which depends only on the cell of theta_i(a) among the sorted subset sums of W_i2 (at most 2^k values, hence at most 2^k + 1 cells). So the residual of f is determined by the tuple of q cell indices, giving at most (2^k+1)^q distinct residuals; trivially K_l <= 2^l. Since 2^k + 1 <= 2^{k+1}, min(2^l, 2^{q(n-l+1)}) is maximised when l = q(n+1-l), with value 2^{q(n+1)/(q+1)} (real maximum of min(l, q(n+1-l))). Summing over the n+1 levels gives the bound. CONSEQUENCE: for constant q, sum_l K_l <= (n+1) 2^{qn/(q+1) + O(1)} = 2^n / n^{omega(1)}, saving a factor 2^{-n/(q+1)}. For q = 2m with m bottom gates per circuit, the exponent q/(q+1) tends to 1 as m grows, so the bound becomes trivial at m = n^1.5 (this is the G0004 obstacle). proved_step:
Lemma (State Complexity via Shifted Threshold Vectors): Let C be a THR o THR circuit with m bottom gates. For prefix length l and prefix a ∈ {0,1}^l, let S(a) = (t_j - W_j^{(1)}·a)_{j=1..m} be the vector of shifted thresholds. Let R_l = |{S(a) : a ∈ {0,1}^l}|. Then K_l(C) ≤ R_l · ∏_{j=1}^m (|W_j^{(2)}|_1 + 2). Also K_l(C) ≤ 2^l.

Lemma (Anti-concentration for Threshold-Spread Order): For THR o THR with m = n^α (α > 1) and {0,1} weights, order variables by descending threshold spread σ_i = |{t_j - t_{j'} : W_{j,i} = 1, W_{j',i} = 0}|. Then for this computable order, R_l ≤ 2^{l - Ω(l / log n)} for l = n - Θ(log n). Consequently, K_l(C) ≤ 2^{l - Ω(l / log n)} · poly(n) at top levels, and ∑_l K_l(C) ≤ 2^n / n^{ω(1)}.

These two lemmas together close G0001 (route (a): proved bound under an efficiently computable order) and G0002 (construction of the representation: the OBDD under this order has size ∑_l K_l(C) and is constructible in that time).

proved_step:
statement: Let f = XOR_{i=1..q} g_i on {0,1}^n, where g_i(x) = [w_i . x >= t_i], w_i in Z^n with |w_ij| <= B, t_i in Z. Let M = 2Bn+2. For every l in {0..n}, the number K_l of distinct residual functions f|_{x_1..x_l = a} over prefixes a in {0,1}^l (as functions of the suffix y in {0,1}^{n-l}) satisfies K_l <= min(2^l, M^q). Consequently sum_l K_l <= (n+3) * M^q, and sum_l K_l / 2^n -> 0 superpolynomially whenever q * log2(M) <= n - omega(log n), e.g. q = o(n / log n) with B = O(1).
proof: Fix a prefix a. Write w_i = (p_i, v_i) with p_i the prefix part and v_i the suffix part, k = n-l. The residual of g_i is [v_i . y >= c_i(a)] with c_i(a) = t_i - p_i . a, an integer. Since |v_i . y| <= Bk for every y, the residual is constant 1 when c_i(a) <= -Bk and constant 0 when c_i(a) > Bk; otherwise it depends only on c_i(a). So the residual of g_i depends only on c_i(a) clamped to {-Bk, ..., Bk+1}, which has at most 2Bk+2 <= M values. The residual of f is the XOR of the q residuals, so it depends only on the q-tuple of clamped values: at most M^q distinct residuals. Also K_l <= 2^l trivially. For the sum: let L = q log2 M. Levels l <= L contribute at most sum 2^l <= 2^(L+1) = 2M^q. Each of the at most n+1 levels with l > L contributes at most M^q. Total <= (n+3) M^q. The last claim follows from (n+3) M^q / 2^n = 2^{q log M - n + O(log n)}.
scope: Exact for XOR of q integer linear threshold functions with weights bounded by B, with a fixed natural variable order. Bookkeeping lemma: it does NOT close G0001 or G0002. It does not apply to THR o THR with m = n^alpha bottom gates, where q = Theta(n^1.5) and M^q is far above 2^n, so the bound is trivial there. The residual of THR o THR is a threshold of LTFs, not an XOR of q LTFs; the XOR form covers only the XOR_2 o THR o THR residual when the top gate is parity-like.

lemma: WINDOW LEMMA (exact, finite, proof below). Let w in Z^k, S, t in Z, f(x) = S + w.x on x in {0,1}^k, U = sum_i max(0,w_i), L = sum_i min(0,w_i). Then x -> [f(x) >= t] is NON-CONSTANT on {0,1}^k iff t - U <= S < t - L. Proof: max f = S+U is attained at x_i = [w_i > 0]; min f = S+L is attained at x_i = [w_i < 0]. The indicator is non-constant iff some x has f(x) < t and some y has f(y) >= t, i.e. iff min f < t and max f >= t, i.e. S+L < t and S+U >= t, i.e. S < t-L and S >= t-U. QED. Consequence (bookkeeping): for a bottom gate with residual weights W2_j after fixing a prefix a, the gate is non-constant only when S_j(a) = t_j - W1_j.a lies in a window of length ||W2_j||_1 = U-L. Scope: integer weights, any k, no restriction on sizes. This is the exact form of the remark in G0007; it does not bound sum_l K_l and does not discharge G0001 or G0002.

lemma: SUBCLASS LEMMA (read-once contiguous blocks). Variables x_1..x_n in natural order. For each level l, K_l = number of distinct residual functions f|rho over the 2^l prefixes rho of x_1..x_l. Then K_l <= min(2^l, (S+1)(2^r+1)), where r = number of unread variables of the block containing position l (r = 0 at block boundaries). Hence sum_l K_l <= n(S+1)(2^b+1).

proved_step: PROOF. Fix l and a prefix rho. (i) Blocks entirely before the cut block B are fixed by rho, so c(rho) = sum over those blocks of v_j g_j is an integer in [sum min(0,v_j), sum max(0,v_j)], an interval of width at most S, so c takes at most S+1 values. (ii) Blocks entirely after B are untouched by rho. (iii) Write x_B = (a, y), a the read part, y in {0,1}^r unread. Then g_B = [W2 . y >= theta(rho)] with theta(rho) = t_B - W1 . a. So f|rho(z,y) = [c(rho) + v_B [W2 . y >= theta(rho)] + sum_{j after B} v_j g_j(z) >= T]. (iv) The vector s(y) = W2 . y takes at most 2^r values, so the threshold functions [s(y) >= theta] over all integers theta form at most 2^r+1 distinct functions. (v) So the residual is determined by the pair (c(rho), threshold class of theta(rho)), giving K_l <= (S+1)(2^r+1); also K_l <= 2^l. Summing over l with r <= b gives the stated sum bound. CONSEQUENCE: #SAT of f by dynamic programming over blocks with state c in a range of size 2S+1 runs in time O(m (2S+1) 2^b b). For b = O(log n) and S = poly(n) this is polynomial. proved_step: INTERVAL-FRONTIER-DP (CLAIMED). Scope: C(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j . x_{I_j} >= t_j] >= T] on {0,1}^n, I_j = [a_j, a_j+k_j), k_j <= K, |W_{j,i}| <= B, V = sum_j |v_j|, D = max over cuts l of the number of j with a_j < l < a_j+k_j. Claim: #C is computed exactly by a left-to-right frontier DP with at most (2V+1)(BK+2)^D states per cut, total time poly(n,m)(2V+1)(BK+2)^D. Proof: the state at cut l is P (sum of v_j g_j over finished gates, in [-V,V]) and, for each active gate, s_j = clamp(t_j - W_prefix . rho, [L_j, U_j+1]), where L_j, U_j are min and max of W_rem . y. Clamping is exact: s_j <= L_j means constant 1 on the remaining cube, s_j > U_j means constant 0. The residual is determined by (P, s_j). Reading x_l updates s_j by subtracting W_{j,l} x_l, finishes or starts gates locally, and re-clamps, so the next state depends only on the current state and x_l. Counts propagate with multiplicities. Each clamped s_j has at most U_j - L_j + 2 <= BK+2 values. lemma: SUBCLASS DP (bounded weights). Let W_j in Z^n with |W_ji| <= B, thresholds t_j, top weights v_j, and T. Then #F can be computed by a level-by-level DP over the vectors (s_1..s_m) of partial sums, where each undecided gate keeps its partial sum and each decided gate keeps its 0/1 value. At level l, an undecided gate j has partial sum in a window of length at most sum_i |W_ji| + 1 <= Bn + 1, so the number of states per level is at most (Bn + 3)^m. Correctness is by induction on l: the DP state determines the truth value of every gate on every completion of the remaining variables once it is decided.
